findings.location: architecture/w02-notes-errata/README.md line 54 ('None of them breaks the binding'); effective/native-profile-v3/README.md lines 42-44 (row R6-3a new text: 'add bound pairs, which no longer break the binding ... every bound grammar pair breaks both'); native-profile-v3-r6-3-vectors.json intents of R63-02 to R63-20 ('so only its own rule is broken')
findings.finding: The round-2 rewording for C1-2 is false for R63-02 and R63-04. The binding (check_record line 258) compares the maintenance words with every unit word removed against the enrolled words. Both enrolled entries already hold systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target (bound pairs of V47 and V52), so after the filter the maintenance list lacks that word and cannot equal the enrolled list. No pair built from V47 or V52 can satisfy the binding. Rule-by-rule evaluation of the vectors: R63-02 breaks the enrolled grammar, the twice-named rule and the binding, but NOT the maintenance grammar, because its only out-of-grammar word is the unit word, which that rule exempts. R63-04 breaks the enrolled grammar, the maintenance grammar ('--'), the twice-named rule and the binding. R63-03, R63-05 to R63-20 and R63-28 to R63-35 break exactly the two grammar rules. Only R63-01 breaks one rule (lockdown). A mutant with only the enrolled grammar off confirms this: R63-02 moves to 'names the maintenance target twice' and R63-04 to 'maintenance boot entry outside the closed kernel parameters'. So these statements are untrue: 'None of them breaks the binding', 'bound pairs, which no longer break the binding' and 'every bound grammar pair breaks both' (fails for R63-02). The 20 vector intents saying 'so only its own rule is broken' are untrue for R63-02 to R63-20. The equivalence statement itself is correct: under the binding, the two grammar rules are equivalent, and the target rule is implied by the twice-named rule.
findings.requiredChange: State that R63-02 and R63-04 cannot be bound: the binding removes every unit word, so an enrolled entry that holds the unit always breaks it. Both also break the twice-named rule; R63-04 also breaks the maintenance grammar, and R63-02 does not. Limit 'no longer break the binding' and 'breaks both grammar rules' to R63-03, R63-05 to R63-20 and R63-28 to R63-35. Correct the R63-02 to R63-20 intents, then update addedVectors.sha256 and source-index.

findings.location: native-profile-v3-errata.json row R6-1d (new text); effective/native-profile-v3/README.md K1 limits, credentials bullet ('so they take effect only if they decrypt'); errata README R6-1 paragraph
findings.finding: The C1-1 rewording is literally true but reads as a protection that systemd v256 gives only conditionally. In systemd v256, the generator that turns systemd.extra-unit.* and systemd.unit-dropin.* credentials into units is debug-generator.c, which reads both credential directories (lines 272-276). It calls read_credential_with_decryption, and that calls decrypt_credential_and_warn without CREDENTIAL_ALLOW_NULL (creds-util.c lines 204-212). A credential sealed with the fixed null key (CRED_AES256_GCM_BY_NULL) carries no secret, so anyone who can write the ESP can produce one. systemd accepts it unless the machine has a TPM2 AND Secure Boot is enabled (creds-util.c lines 1221-1238). With TPM2 present and Secure Boot off, it accepts it with only a warning. So on a machine without a TPM2, or with Secure Boot off, ESP-placed /.extra/credentials and /.extra/global_credentials 'decrypt' and take effect. The K1 limits list is meant to enumerate what the binding does not exclude, so this condition belongs there.
findings.requiredChange: Add the null-key condition, for example: '... so they take effect only if they decrypt; a credential sealed with systemd's null key, which anyone with write access to the ESP can produce, decrypts unless the machine has a TPM2 and Secure Boot is enabled'. Alternatively, drop 'so they take effect only if they decrypt'.
